additionalDonationProof.scope: Pre-existing Router/Pool PASS/USDC dust and predicted future Pool donations before final Mint. Neither resulted in donation DoS or LP diversion.

newFindings.rationale: The equality validates the token balance difference across one exact pull/send, including claim/funding/proceeds/Vault venue paths, rather than an absolute balance. A donation completed before entry increases both sides of the captured baseline and cancels from the difference. Fixed non-rebasing test tokens have no callback that allows a third party to interleave another transaction during settlement; mismatching transfers revert atomically. Existing donation and bad-delivery fixtures and the focused dust tests support this boundary.

All other equalities compare exact token balance differences to the signed/actual settled amount. The fixed test tokens have no transfer callbacks. Local test test_PreExistingRouterAndPoolDustDoesNotBlockNativeBuyOrSell passed with pre-existing PASS and USDC in both Router and Pool; Router dust remains unchanged after both ETH directions.

The reported equality compares protocol getReserves() to the configured initial 500k PASS / 250k USDC and fresh LP ownership to newly minted shares. Pool.initialize accepts physical balance >= configured reserve. Native/USDC pre-donations to the predicted CREATE address leave accounting reserves and LP ownership intact. Local test test_PreFundedPredictedPoolDoesNotBlockFinalMintOrStealInitialLP passed.

The compared LP token is created during this transaction and has zero pre-existing supply; caller initializer and configured recipient are explicit. PASS/USDC transferred before predicted deployment cannot create LP balances. Local predicted-address donation test passed and verified all initial LP supply equals the configured recipient share balance.

All externally reachable settlement entries for this reported function use the same pinned OpenZeppelin nonReentrant guard. FairLaunch._launch is private and reached only from guarded subscribeUsdc/subscribeEth. StrategyVault.execute and inherited deposit/withdraw/close share the inherited guard. State writes occur after a guarded trusted-reserve call and revert atomically on failure.

Assembly is limited to validated ECDSA calldata reads or immutable bytecode chunk storage/reconstruction/CREATE. Signature length/low-s/v checks precede ecrecover. Vault factory chunks are created by the constructor, prefixed STOP, and never user selected; CREATE uses fixed reviewed code plus typed configuration with caller owner. No delegatecall or writable user-address target.
